activity.notes: Moytoy was an influential headman of Great Tellico. In 1730 Alexander Cuming orchestrated a ceremony styling him 'Emperor of the Cherokee', but Cherokee towns retained their own councils and leadership and the title did not create a centralized Cherokee monarchy. ATLAS therefore records his actual Great Tellico leadership and preserves the colonial 'emperor' title only in the notes.

sources.title: Moytoy of Tellico
sources.citation_text: The compiled biography identifies Moytoy as a Cherokee leader from Great Tellico, records the British-engineered 1730 'Emperor' ceremony, and his death in 1741.

sources.title: Moytoy's Folly — Georgia Tribe of Eastern Cherokee
sources.citation_text: The tribal history emphasizes that Cherokee communities remained self-governing and describes Moytoy as an influential respected headman rather than a genuine centralized emperor.
